evals.prompt: Import the supplied stripped C++ fixture into Ghidra through AETHER and perform a complete whole-binary annotation. Rename all application functions appropriately, preserve runtime/library functions, recover its classes, virtual methods, and high-confidence object fields, and keep a resumable PROGRESS.md. Continue until every function and structure candidate has a recorded disposition. Save PROGRESS.md and a compact verification.json listing the final function names and recovered structures to the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A complete, resumable annotation of the C++ fixture with namespace-aware methods, consistent virtual-family names, conservative comments, recovered object fields, and complete coverage accounting.
expectations: PROGRESS.md exists and records a disposition for every discovered function with zero default-named application functions remaining
verification.json is valid JSON listing final function names and recovered structures
Virtual-family methods share consistent names across the abstract base and derived class (parse/reset/destructor), and the fixture namespace is preserved in method names
The shared packet/state structure is recovered with semantic high-confidence field names (data/length/cursor-offset/valid) rather than generic offset names
Runtime/library/import functions are preserved or canonicalized with evidence rather than left default-named or semantically renamed

evals.prompt: Fully annotate the supplied stripped C fixture with AETHER Ghidra. Examine every function, distinguish application code from compiler/runtime/library code, use conservative C naming, recover the shared state structures and only high-confidence semantic fields, and track all work in PROGRESS.md so the run can resume after interruption. Save PROGRESS.md and verification.json to the output directory.
evals.expected_output: Exhaustive C annotation with safe symbol preservation, evidence-backed function names/comments, recovered shared structures, and no unaccounted functions.
expectations: PROGRESS.md exists with complete coverage counts and a disposition row for every discovered function
verification.json is valid JSON listing final names and the recovered structure
Application functions receive conservative snake_case C names derived from evidence (init/consume/close pattern) with confidence comments
A shared connection/state structure is recovered with high-confidence semantic fields including an 8-byte counter field and a 32-byte name buffer
Compiler/runtime/import/thunk functions are preserved or canonicalized rather than semantically renamed

evals.prompt: Perform whole-binary annotation on the supplied Go executable using AETHER Ghidra. Preserve all identified Go package, method, runtime, wrapper, and ABI symbols; improve understanding with confidence-labeled function comments rather than renaming those symbols. Review every function and recover only strongly evidenced structures/fields. Maintain PROGRESS.md and save it with verification.json in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: Complete Go-aware coverage that does not rename reliable Go symbols, adds evidence-based confidence comments, preserves runtime functions, and records all progress and structure decisions.
expectations: PROGRESS.md exists and accounts for every discovered function including unnamed FUN_ functions with counts and dispositions
Zero renames applied to identified Go package, method, runtime, wrapper, or ABI symbols
Confidence-labeled comments in [Confidence: ...] format with Purpose/Evidence are applied instead of renaming Go symbols
Only strongly evidenced structures are created, with any low-evidence fields left generic and explicitly tracked
